paper.title: UAV-VLRR: Vision-Language Informed NMPC for Rapid Response in UAV Search and Rescue
paper.central_claim: UAV-VLRR cascades GPT-4o + Molmo-7B target/obstacle extraction from one aerial image-text pair with an onboard point-to-point NMPC with obstacle penalty, giving faster SAR mission completion: on average 33.75% faster than an off-the-shelf autopilot and 54.6% faster than a human pilot (two scenes).
paper.claim_scope_note: Conclusion wording 'outperforms other traditional approaches in the field of drone search and rescue' exceeds the evidence: one indoor arena, two static scenes, one timed flight per method per scene.

preliminary_judgment: Written before opening seat totals. Operation: a frozen LLM (GPT-4o) names targets/obstacles and a 4-bit Molmo-7B returns pixel points from one aerial image + instruction; pixels are scaled to metric coordinates with camera height/FoV (flat-ground, top-down assumption); a 13-state point-to-point NMPC (CasADi, RK4 multiple shooting, obstacle penalty) flies to the points onboard. The LLM is used once, open loop; there is no feedback from execution to the extraction. Evidence: Vicon vs detected coordinates for 12 objects (per-axis errors; 25 cm radial criterion), and Table III gives one mission time per method per scene (28/40/57 s and 30/48/72 s). Exp1 and Exp2 share the multimodal setup ('the multimodal setup (Experiments 1 and 2)'), so Exp1 vs Exp2 is a one-factor controller swap, but the autopilot is unnamed and its configuration/timing start undisclosed. No mission-success criterion, no trial counts, no repeats, no collision counts for UAV-VLRR, human timing starts at image display. Initial view: in scope (frontier LLM/VLM composed with a controller for a UAV), mechanism plausible, evidence thin and single-trial; strongest supportable claim is two timed static-arena flights faster than an unnamed autopilot.

evidence.support_explanation: Frozen frontier planner separates semantic selection from geometric control.

evidence.quote: their pixel coordinates are mapped onto the image and converted into real-world coordinates using image metadata.
evidence.support_explanation: Geometric handoff uses height/FoV, not learned end-to-end control.

evidence.quote: The NMPC finds the optimal trajectory and the set of control inputs designed for rapid control.
evidence.support_explanation: Point-to-point control takes target/obstacle coordinates; constrained optimization is delegated.

evidence.quote: Each experiment was timed to assess the speed of execution.
evidence.support_explanation: Timing protocol starts at code launch versus image shown to pilot; mission objective specified but no numerical flight-completion threshold.

evidence.quote: For this analysis, an identification was considered accurate if the detected point was within a 25 cm radius of the actual object.
evidence.support_explanation: Ground-truth Vicon checks coordinate identification, not a repeated mission-success audit.

evidence.quote: Time Taken for Scene 1 (s) 28 40 57 Time Taken for Scene 2 (s) 30 48 72
evidence.support_explanation: Two scene timings, not trial-counted success rates; no variance.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In two static indoor-arena scenes, one timed flight each: GPT-4o+Molmo coordinates executed by onboard point-to-point NMPC finished in 28 s / 30 s, vs 40 / 48 s for an unnamed autopilot on the same targets and 57 / 72 s for a human pilot; Vicon errors near the 25 cm criterion (11/12 within radially).
assessment.evidence_level_reason: EVIDENCE.md online requires closed-loop success judged by execution with per-task trial counts and success rates for real robots; here no success criterion, no trial counts, no success rates are reported, only single timed flights, so the strict online bar is not met (rule 1: judge by evidence).

G.reason: Real limitation (manual waypoint setting slow; trajectory-tracking NMPC needs offboard compute) with nearest lineage named (UAV-VLA, ETH NMPC line), but the bottleneck is not diagnosed and the residue vs UAV-VLA is only textual. Both seats agree.

M.reason: Specific mechanism with partial causal rationale (point-to-point NMPC tolerates model mismatch, runs onboard, consumes points directly), but key assumptions are weak and unexamined: flat-ground height/FoV scaling from a single image, one-shot extraction with no verification, static obstacles, unspecified obstacle-penalty form. Anchor 2 (key assumptions thin), not 3.

X.reason: Main steps reconstructible (LLM -> VLM -> geometry -> NMPC); prompts, penalty, weights, horizon, goal tolerance, autopilot configuration and failure handling missing. Both seats agree.

measurement.reason: Anchors v2: mission success/reach criterion undefined and no trial denominator (one flight per cell, none counted) -> 0-1. Credit to 1 for objective timing and the 12-object Vicon perception check.

causality.reason: Exp1 vs Exp2 holds the multimodal targets fixed and swaps only the controller (agg:E001), a genuine one-factor control; unseparated confound remains in the undisclosed autopilot configuration, and the extraction stage and human comparison are uncontrolled. Matches anchor 2 (control exists, key confound unseparated).

holdout.reason: Two scenes in one arena with one instruction; tuning scenes undisclosed; no unseen environment or embodiment. Both seats agree.

statistics.reason: Anchors v2: no repeats and no failure breakdown -> <=1; per-object error table credits 1. Both seats agree.

cost.reason: Central metric is wall-clock with VLRR timed from code launch (inference latency included); call budget is inferable (one LLM + one VLM call per mission); hardware disclosed. Missing latency breakdown, API/token cost and autopilot timing start. Matches anchor 2 (budget inferable, parts unpriced), above 1 (hardware only).

resolutions.reason: EVIDENCE.md: real-robot online requires per-task trial counts and success rates. Neither is reported (son55 itself notes no success/collision definition and n=1). Real flights exist but are timed single runs; strict rule 1 withholds online.

resolutions.reason: Format difference only; both read the complete fixed material.

C25's load-bearing tactic is closing the loop with the solver's verifiable output during construction; son55's own step check marks step 3 and step 4 as missing. Extraction is one-shot with no feedback, so no sub-card applies.

Anchor 3/4 needs assumptions reconstructible with distinguishable predictions; here flat-ground scaling, one-shot unverified extraction, static obstacles and the penalty form are untested or unspecified (sol's own reason concedes these limit guarantees).
Anchors v2 clause 'criterion and denominator both absent -> 0-1' applies: no reach/success criterion and no counted trials; sol applied only the single-trial <=2 ceiling.

son55's premise that shared target points are unstated is contradicted by V-B ('the multimodal setup (Experiments 1 and 2)'); Exp1/2 is a one-factor controller swap with a residual confound (autopilot configuration), which is anchor 2.
The timed metric itself includes inference (timer starts at code launch) and the call budget is inferable; this exceeds 'hardware only'. Missing breakdown and autopilot timing start keep it at 2.

resolutions.reason: The paper's criterion is a 25 cm radius; Table II per-axis 23/10 cm gives about 25.1 cm radially (our_inference). Not in conflicts.json but a factual error in son55's strongest claim.
